description:
TIPS: Submit a tip: 
https://midwest.clickup.com/forms/9006119175/p/f/8ccwy87-63537/H3BKH5EZAPIBRYJ1XB/tips

PRIVACY or COMPLAINTS: Privacy concern or other issue:
https://midwest.clickup.com/forms/9006119175/f/8ccwy87-63557/LE0PT31DZVHHEIE5AW

EMAIL US: contact@midwest-safety.com

MERCH: Midwest-Safety.com

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: contact@midwest-safety.com

There's one in the, two in the chest. Okay, bud? Yeah, that's right. No, just me. I'm going to go off date. This incident took place in Boise, Idaho on November 13th, 2024. The suspect, 22-year-old Gabriel Pope, was shot three times during the incident and was quickly provided medical aid before being transported to a nearby hospital. The officer who fired the three shots, Boise Police Corporal Steve Martinez, was placed on administrative leave after the shooting, while an investigation was opened into whether he was justified or not. Pope, after being treated at the hospital, survived his injuries and was later charged with felony aggravated assault on law enforcement, resisting arrest and providing false identification to law enforcement. Pope's attorney said that he has had a very traumatic life, as his mental health issues have caused him to commit crimes throughout his whole life, even while he was a minor. In September 2025, 10 months after the incident, as part of a plea deal, Pope pleaded guilty to aggravated assault on law enforcement with an enhancement for use of a deadly weapon during the commission of a felony while the other charges were dropped. The judge, who told Pope he needed to, quote, grow up, sentenced him to 10 years in prison with the possibility for parole after four years. She also urged the Idaho Department of Correction to provide mental health counseling, aggression, and substance abuse treatment during his incarceration. In November 2025, a full year after the incident, prosecutors found the officer who shot Pope justified in his decision under Idaho law after reviewing the body cam footage. You want to know how fast a normal day can turn into a life or death situation in seconds, and sometimes it starts with a seatbelt violation. A traffic stop feels normal to the public, but to officers is one of the most unpredictable things we can do. Because the second passengers start reaching, hiding, or ignoring instructions, the officer's brain has to shift from paperwork to survival and not because they want to it's because they have to some people might miss this but during a traffic stop the officer isn't just watching the driver he's watching every pair of hands in that car so you don't reach you don't argue and you definitely don't create confusion because one person moving when told not to can put everyone in danger inside their car And we even see how chaotic it becomes because someone stepping out at the wrong time can unknowingly move into an officer's line of fire. Keep in mind, when someone runs and they're armed, officers don't know intentions. They reap behavior. And a person advancing with a knife closes distance faster than most people realize. At that moment, an officer isn't judging a person's life. He's reacting to an immediate threat. Part that sits heavy with me is sometimes a person coming at you is clearly struggling mentally. If that doesn't make the danger smaller, it makes the decision harder. And yes, the officer goes home alive, but he carries the choice he never wanted to make.
